currentContext.business: Coromandel offers an integrated portfolio across the agricultural value chain spanning plant nutrients, crop protection, specialty and organic solutions, retail and agri services, designed to improve farm productivity and profitability. It operates a pan-India network of 18 manufacturing plants producing fertilisers, crop protection products, biologicals, water soluble fertilisers and nano products, backed by backward integration into critical raw materials, intermediates and captive utilities. Its products and services reach approximately 2 crore farmers annually through roughly 1,200 rural retail outlets, digital platforms and on-ground agronomists offering soil testing, crop diagnostics, farm mechanisation support and agronomic advisory.

currentContext.expansion: Coromandel deployed capital expenditure of about Rs. 1,300 crore during FY 2025-26, primarily directed towards backward integration and capacity expansion. Key backward integration projects, including the sulphuric acid and phosphoric acid plants at Kakinada, were commissioned during the year, enhancing supply security and reducing dependence on imports. The Company is on track to commission a 7.5 lakh ton NPK granulation plant at Kakinada, which will establish it as one of the largest integrated phosphatics complexes in the country. Upstream, the Senegal rock phosphate project operated through Baobab Mining and Chemicals Corporation (BMCC) delivered an operational turnaround with its highest-ever production and exports of rock phosphate, and Coromandel increased its equity stake in BMCC to 71.5% to strengthen strategic control and secure long-term raw material access; the Company also emerged as the largest exporter of rock phosphate from Senegal. In crop protection, capacity augmentation plus the completed acquisition of a 53% stake in NACL Industries Limited expanded manufacturing capabilities and distribution reach in domestic and international markets. Ongoing investments continue in crop protection, speciality nutrients, water-soluble fertilisers and new product development, which management expects to support future growth and margin expansion. Speciality Nutrients strengthened manufacturing capabilities for key products and expanded into new geographies. Downstream, the retail network was expanded to approximately 1,200 outlets, and drone-based spraying coverage through Gromor Drive and Retail reached about 2.9 lakh acres during the year. A joint venture, Stuccoedge India Private Limited, was formed through a wholly owned subsidiary for the manufacture and sale of phospho-gypsum-based products. Manufacturing performance included record production of phosphatics fertilisers of 35.3 LMT along with higher phosphoric acid volumes, with the Kakinada unit receiving the British Safety Council 'Sword of Honour' award.

risks.risk: Raw material price escalation and input cost inflation
risks.note: FY 2025-26 saw a sharp escalation in raw material prices, particularly in the second half, increasing cost pressures across the value chain; fertiliser inputs and energy prices firmed even as broader commodity markets stayed stable.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption to fertiliser input supply and shipping
risks.note: Supply disruptions from the Middle East and China, unplanned outages and logistics bottlenecks tightened availability of ammonia, urea, sulphur and phosphates; shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea keep global supply chains under pressure and freight/energy costs elevated into FY27.

risks.risk: Monsoon and weather dependence, including a transition to El Nino
risks.note: Erratic distribution and delayed withdrawal of the southwest monsoon affected crop cycles and rural consumption in October-November; a transition to El Nino conditions could bring drier conditions across key agricultural regions and hit crop yields.

risks.risk: Concentrated phosphate supply and China export restrictions
risks.note: Phosphate markets stayed tight amid China's export restrictions and high input costs, while potash firmed on supply constraints and geopolitical risk — a direct exposure for a phosphatics-led producer.

risks.risk: Demand slowdown and softening agri-commodity realisations
risks.note: The year was impacted by a slowdown in consumption demand; Indian Agri GDP growth moderated to about 3% (from 4.2%) on uneven climatic conditions and softening food commodity prices, and global fertiliser demand growth was constrained by lower crop realisations, high interest rates and currency pressures.

Sector economics rest on government policy — crop insurance, interest subvention, PM-AASHA price support, PM-KISAN income support and fertiliser policy; global markets are described as highly sensitive to policy changes and interventions.

Delays in the IMO net-zero framework and a phased, uneven rollout of carbon border adjustment mechanisms (CBAM) led to deferment or reassessment of certain low-carbon fertiliser projects, creating investment-timing uncertainty; green hydrogen/green ammonia shifts have long-term implications for the fertiliser industry.

risks.risk: Trade protectionism and tariffs on Indian exports
risks.note: The United States imposed reciprocal and additional tariffs on Indian exports during the year, introducing uncertainty in export markets and accelerating supply-chain diversification and regionalisation.

Despite strong Indian macro fundamentals, the currency remained influenced by elevated US interest rates, geopolitical uncertainty and global commodity market volatility, affecting import-dependent raw material costs.

one-line thesis: Coromandel delivered record operational volumes and diversified earnings via NACL integration, but Q4 PAT was severely impacted by one-off impairments and prior-year land sale comparables. The critical near-term pivot is the mismatch between soaring global raw material costs (Ammonia/Sulphur) due to Middle East tensions and lagging government subsidy revisions, creating margin uncertainty for Q1/Q2FY27 despite strong volume growth.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 6,068cr (+19% YoY); EBITDA: INR 494cr (+16% YoY, margin ~8.1%); PAT (Reported): INR 115cr (-80% YoY) vs PAT (Normalized/Op): Significantly higher excluding one-offs; Order Book: N/A (FMCG/Agri model); Net Debt: Not explicitly quantified but NACL rights issue (INR 250cr) utilized to reduce high-cost debt. One-offs: Current year INR 71cr impairment on drone investments vs Prior Year INR 347cr exceptional gain from land sale, creating a ~INR 420cr headline distortion.
guidance: Revenue Growth: 20-25% expected in Crop Protection; Margin: Fertilizer margins under pressure until subsidy revision (Q2 uncertainty), Crop Protection sustaining ~19%; Order Inflow: Strong summer sowing demand; Capex/Commissioning: Kakinada acid plants stabilizing, Granulation plant by Dec FY27.
order book & pipeline: N/A - Business operates on continuous production and channel inventory; Finished Goods Inventory: ~5.5 lakh tons (incl. ~60k-70k trading).
segment / subsidiary detail: Fertilizers: Record sales 4.3MT (+7%), Market Share 17.5%, Unique Grades 35%. Crop Protection (Standalone): Rev INR 3,054cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 569cr (+55%), Margin ~19%. NACL (Consolidated): Rev INR 1,585cr (+28%), EBITDA INR 103cr (turnaround from loss), Margin 6-7% (targeting 9-10%). Specialty/Nano: Nano DAP vol +60%, 50% market share.
growth verticals / optionality: Senegal mine volume increase (30-40%); New technical capacity at Dahej/Sarigam; Retail expansion (300 new stores); Drone services scaling; New product launches (10 new CP products).
margins & cost dynamics: Fertilizer: Compressed due to raw material spike (Ammonia ~$840-850, Sulphur ~$800) vs fixed NBS rates; awaiting govt pass-through. Crop Protection: Robust (~19%) supported by export mix, currency depreciation, and pricing power on Mancozeb.
capex / expansion: INR 3,000cr invested over last 2 years; Key projects: Kakinada Sulphuric (2k TPD) & Phosphoric (650 TPD) acid plants (commissioned March, stabilizing); Granulation plant (Dec FY27 commissioning); Senegal mining expansion.
capital allocation: Rights issue (INR 250cr) for NACL to deleverage; Focus on synergy realization between Coromandel and NACL; Prudent impairment taken on Dhaksha (drone) subsidiary to clean up balance sheet.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical disruption in Strait of Hormuz affecting 80%+ import dependence for Ammonia/Sulphur; Delay in government subsidy revision for Kharif 2026; Erratic monsoon forecast (below normal predicted); Inventory valuation losses if RM prices correct sharply.
management quality / tone: Operationally confident on volumes and integration success; Cautious/Prudent on near-term fertilizer margins due to external macro/geopolitical factors; Transparent about one-off accounting distortions.
non-obvious takeaways: The reported PAT collapse is almost entirely accounting-driven (land sale comp + impairment), masking strong operational cash generation; NACL's margin expansion is capped at ~9-10% until new formulation registrations mature, limiting immediate consolidated margin upside despite revenue scale.

themes.title: Fertilizer subsidy & nutrient-policy cycle
themes.need: Fertilizer makers are driven by NBS/urea subsidy policy, gas-pooling and nutrient pricing rather than the crop-protection volume/molecule-launch recovery. Q1FY27's supply-side read comes from MBAPL: revenue roughly flat at INR 416cr with EBITDA +16% and PAT +17% purely on cheap March-bought raw material that management said is now EXHAUSTED, with utilisation only ~43-45% because of raw-material availability rather than demand - SSP sales were +28% and NPK +33% YoY against production down 7%/28%. Its Dhule (Maharashtra) integrated complex commissions +3,30,000 MTPA DAP-NPK plus 99,000 MTPA phosphoric acid in Oct-2026 and a second phase in Oct-2027, framed as a >50% turnover jump toward ~INR 3,500cr revenue and 15.6 lakh MT capacity by FY28; Egypt/Jordan rock-phosphate sourcing (non-Hormuz) insulated it relative to import-dependent peers. Subsidy clarity and gas costs still set the near-term margin.
themes.driver: NBS/urea subsidy policy (the Oct-Mar rate revision), gas-pooling and nutrient pricing; MBAPL's Oct-2026 Dhule commissioning and the utilisation ramp toward ~90%; kharif demand pull-through after a delayed monsoon.

hero.oneLiner: Coromandel International is one of India's leading integrated agri-solutions companies and the country's leading private sector manufacturer and marketer of phosphatic fertilisers, combining pan-India manufacturing with last-mile rural retail reach.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Coromandel International is one of India's leading integrated agri-solutions companies and the country's leading private sector manufacturer and marketer of phosphatic fertilisers, combining pan-India manufacturing with last-mile rural retail reach.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Coromandel offers an integrated portfolio across the agricultural value chain spanning plant nutrients, crop protection, specialty and organic solutions, retail and agri services, designed to improve farm productivity and profitability. It operates a pan-India network of 18 manufacturing plants producing fertilisers, crop protection products, biologicals, water soluble fertilisers and nano products, backed by backward integration into critical raw materials, intermediates and captive utilities. Its products and services reach approximately 2 crore farmers annually through roughly 1,200 rural retail outlets, digital platforms and on-ground agronomists offering soil testing, crop diagnostics, farm mechanisation support and agronomic advisory.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- NACL Industries Limited — related party: Arun Alagappan is Non-Executive Chairman of NACL Industries Limited alongside his role as Executive Chairman of Coromandel
- Tunisian Indian Fertiliser S.A. (Tunisia) — JV: The Managing Director & CEO represents Coromandel on its board
- Foskor (Pty) Ltd. (South Africa) — associate: The Managing Director & CEO represents Coromandel on its board
- Baobab rock phosphate mining initiative, Senegal — subsidiary: Backward-integration rock phosphate mining project commissioned under the Executive Chairman's leadership
- Murugappa Group — related party: Promoter group; the Executive Chairman belongs to the fourth generation of the Murugappa family and the Group's philanthropy tradition shapes Coromandel's CSR
- Corporate venture capital arm — subsidiary: Launched under the Executive Chairman's leadership; entity not named in the text

NACL (Consolidated): Rev INR 1,585cr (+28%), EBITDA INR 103cr (turnaround from loss), Margin 6-7% (targeting 9-10%). Specialty/Nano: Nano DAP vol +60%, 50% market share.

guidance.body: Revenue Growth: 20-25% expected in Crop Protection; Margin: Fertilizer margins under pressure until subsidy revision (Q2 uncertainty), Crop Protection sustaining ~19%; Order Inflow: Strong summer sowing demand; Capex/Commissioning: Kakinada acid plants stabilizing, Granulation plant by Dec FY27.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Senegal mine volume increase (30-40%); New technical capacity at Dahej/Sarigam; Retail expansion (300 new stores); Drone services scaling; New product launches (10 new CP products).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Ongoing investments in crop protection, speciality nutrients, water-soluble fertilisers and new product development are expected to support future growth and margin expansion
- Near term, global fertiliser markets are expected to remain tight and volatile, with prices supported primarily by supply-side constraints; demand is expected to remain selective with buyers prioritising supply security and flexible contracting
- Agri-commodity prices in FY27 are expected to be sensitive to the ongoing Middle East conflict, which could influence energy and fertiliser markets and hence farm input costs
- Weather remains a critical monitorable, with a transition to El Nino conditions potentially producing drier conditions across key agricultural regions and affecting crop yields
- Entering FY27, Middle East tensions are expected to keep energy and freight volatility and cost pressures elevated, potentially delaying monetary easing and moderating consumption-led growth in Asia
- Medium-term global agriculture outlook remains structurally positive but with moderating growth (OECD-FAO 2025-2034); emerging markets in Asia and Africa remain the primary drivers of incremental demand
- Adoption of biological solutions is gaining momentum globally with the market expected to scale up significantly, supporting the shift to environmentally sustainable crop inputs
- Biofuels are strengthening the agriculture-energy linkage, influencing cropping patterns and adding volatility to agri-commodity prices
- Indian fertiliser demand supported by structural factors — food security requirements, a large agrarian economy, sustained cropping intensity and continued policy support
- Sector project pipelines for low-carbon/green ammonia fertiliser capacity are expected to accelerate post-2027, driven by structural demand growth and the need to replace ageing capacity
- Indian agriculture is shifting towards diversification (horticulture, oilseeds, pulses), mechanisation (~45% levels) and drone/precision-agriculture adoption, expanding the addressable services opportunity
- Cost headwinds flagged: sharp escalation in raw material prices, particularly in the second half, and a slowdown in consumption demand

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Fertilizer: Compressed due to raw material spike (Ammonia ~$840-850, Sulphur ~$800) vs fixed NBS rates; awaiting govt pass-through. Crop Protection: Robust (~19%) supported by export mix, currency depreciation, and pricing power on Mancozeb.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Rights issue (INR 250cr) for NACL to deleverage; Focus on synergy realization between Coromandel and NACL; Prudent impairment taken on Dhaksha (drone) subsidiary to clean up balance sheet.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Coromandel deployed capital expenditure of about Rs. 1,300 crore during FY 2025-26, primarily directed towards backward integration and capacity expansion. Key backward integration projects, including the sulphuric acid and phosphoric acid plants at Kakinada, were commissioned during the year, enhancing supply security and reducing dependence on imports. The Company is on track to commission a 7.5 lakh ton NPK granulation plant at Kakinada, which will establish it as one of the largest integrated phosphatics complexes in the country. Upstream, the Senegal rock phosphate project operated through Baobab Mining and Chemicals Corporation (BMCC) delivered an operational turnaround with its highest-ever production and exports of rock phosphate, and Coromandel increased its equity stake in BMCC to 71.5% to strengthen strategic control and secure long-term raw material access; the Company also emerged as the largest exporter of rock phosphate from Senegal. In crop protection, capacity augmentation plus the completed acquisition of a 53% stake in NACL Industries Limited expanded manufacturing capabilities and distribution reach in domestic and international markets. Ongoing investments continue in crop protection, speciality nutrients, water-soluble fertilisers and new product development, which management expects to support future growth and margin expansion. Speciality Nutrients strengthened manufacturing capabilities for key products and expanded into new geographies. Downstream, the retail network was expanded to approximately 1,200 outlets, and drone-based spraying coverage through Gromor Drive and Retail reached about 2.9 lakh acres during the year. A joint venture, Stuccoedge India Private Limited, was formed through a wholly owned subsidiary for the manufacture and sale of phospho-gypsum-based products. Manufacturing performance included record production of phosphatics fertilisers of 35.3 LMT along with higher phosphoric acid volumes, with the Kakinada unit receiving the British Safety Council 'Sword of Honour' award.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Deep farmer engagement — products and services reach ~2 crore farmers annually, with the 'Gromor' brand widely recognised for quality and local relevance
- End-to-end agri solutions across soil health, seeds, crop nutrition, crop protection and farm mechanisation, delivered through retail outlets, digital platforms and on-ground agronomists
- Backward-integrated manufacturing across 18 plants including critical raw material sourcing, intermediates production and captive utilities, giving control over cost, quality and operational resilience
- Raw material security through long-term tie-ups, sourcing diversification and captive rock phosphate from the Senegal (BMCC) mine, insulating plants from global supply disruptions
- Market leadership — leading private sector phosphatic fertiliser manufacturer, leadership in POS consumption and market leader in SSP across primary and POS sales
- Strong balance sheet with healthy liquidity, low leverage and consistent cash flows enabling disciplined capital allocation
- Governance anchored in the Murugappa Group's 'Five Lights' — Integrity, Passion, Quality, Respect, Responsibility
- Innovation engine — 19 new products introduced during the year plus a pipeline of new molecules and formulations, with growing focus on biologicals
- Over 60 years of legacy in Indian agriculture

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical disruption in Strait of Hormuz affecting 80%+ import dependence for Ammonia/Sulphur; Delay in government subsidy revision for Kharif 2026; Erratic monsoon forecast (below normal predicted); Inventory valuation losses if RM prices correct sharply.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The reported PAT collapse is almost entirely accounting-driven (land sale comp + impairment), masking strong operational cash generation; NACL's margin expansion is capped at ~9-10% until new formulation registrations mature, limiting immediate consolidated margin upside despite revenue scale.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- 'Consolidate to Accelerate' — consolidate core strengths across businesses, operations and capabilities while building a foundation for future growth
- Backward integration and raw material security: commissioning sulphuric and phosphoric acid plants at Kakinada, stabilising the Senegal rock phosphate mining project, and reducing import dependence
- Scale the Crop Protection business as a growth driver through portfolio expansion, capacity augmentation and a pipeline of new molecules and formulations, reinforced by the 53% stake acquisition in NACL Industries Limited
- Expand direct-to-farmer …
